description.narrative:
The Sahel Integrated Programme for Climate Resilience and Migration aims to empower National Societies in the Sahel, supporting their efforts to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable populations and people on the move in the face of shocks and stresses, particularly those driven or exacerbated by climate change. Country level implementation will be focussed in Burkina Faso, Chad, Mauritania – 3 countries facing converging challenges of environmental degradation, displacement and systemic poverty. The regional component targets the 10 National Societies members of the Sahel+ Platform.
The programme takes a dual approach of response and prevention, recognising the urgent humanitarian needs triggered by climate-related disasters, conflicts and other crises and highlights the importance of strengthening long term adaptation and resilience. Through our Humanitarian Service Point Model, the programme provides essential services to migrants already on the move - many displaced by droughts, floods and the loss of climate-sensitive livelihoods – while strengthening local led and community based systems that create viable alternative options to migration. Locally led approaches such as the Mothers’ Clubs, Farmers field Schools and social protection mechanisms play a central role in this model. These platforms empower communities – to lead climate-informed adaptation efforts: from financial inclusion through climate informed/climate smart income generating activities and climate smart agriculture to early warning dissemination and surveillance data. By improving food security, diversifying livelihoods and increasing access to economic opportunities locally, the programme helps communities adapt to climate change and make informed choices about whether to stay or migrate. Cash-based assistance is embedded across the programme as a preferred, dignified modality – particularly in responding to shocks such as floods, drought or displacement. Whenever feasible, cash will be the preferred modality for delivering support across all activities, including migrant assistance and income-generating initiatives, giving people a dignified way to choose how best to meet their needs scalable, shock-responsive systems will enable timely assistance that protects livelihoods and accelerates climate resilient recovery.
